verses.1: When I came to you, brothers, I did not come with superiority of speech or wisdom, declaring to you the testimony of God.
verses.2: For I resolved to know nothing among you except Jesus the Messiah and him crucified.
verses.3: And I came among you in weakness, in fear, and in great trembling,
verses.4: and my message and my proclamation were not in persuasive wisdom, but in proof of the Spirit and power,
verses.5: so that your faith might not be in the wisdom of humans, but in the power of God.
verses.6: We speak wisdom among the mature, but not the wisdom of this age or the rulers of this age who are being nullified;
verses.7: but we speak God's wisdom in mystery, the wisdom hidden, which God predestined before the ages for our glory;
verses.8: a wisdom no ruler of this age knew, for if he had known, he would not have crucified the Lord of glory.
verses.9: But just as it is written, “What eye has not seen, and ear has not heard, and into the heart of a human has not come, what God has prepared for those who love him.”
verses.10: For God revealed it to us through the Spirit, for the Spirit searches everything, even the depths of God.
verses.11: For who knows the things of a human except the spirit of the human that is in him? So also no one knows the things of God except the Spirit of God.
verses.12: Now we have not received the spirit of the world, but the Spirit from God, that we might know the things given to us by God.
verses.13: And we speak these things not in humanly taught words of wisdom, but in taught words of the Spirit, comparing spiritual things with spiritual.
verses.14: But the natural person does not accept the things of the Spirit of God, for they are foolishness to him, and he cannot understand them, because they are spiritually discerned.
verses.15: But the spiritual person discerns all things, yet is himself discerned by no one.
verses.16: For who has known the mind of the Lord, so as to instruct him? But we have the mind of Christ.

notes:
Notes
- v. 6: “rulers of this age” reflects the Greek “ἀρχόντων τοῦ αἰῶνος τούτου” as spiritual authorities being set aside, not political ones.
- v. 11: “spirit of the human” and “Spirit of God” are differentiated deliberately to emphasize the contrast between the human and divine.
- v. 13: “taught words of the Spirit” and “spiritual things with spiritual” preserve the double use of “πνευματικοῖς” for rhetorical effect.
- v. 16: “mind of Christ” is a deliberate rendering of “νοῦν Χριστοῦ” to avoid overliteralism like “the mind of the Lord.”
